security_audit.summary: All 60 static findings are false positives: they match Markdown formatting, sample task documentation, API references, or a constrained GitHub CLI CI monitor. The review identified two intent-level concerns in SKILL.md: persistent role instructions and an unconditional local autonomy exception that can weaken normal user control.

remediation.suggestion: Make coordinator mode opt-in for each request or allow the user to revoke it at any time. Do not require later requests to be delegated automatically.
Remove the local-path exception. Require explicit confirmation before implementation, command execution, or external actions regardless of the working directory.
Warn users that failed CI logs may contain sensitive data and offer a summary-only mode before printing logs.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent coordinator-mode instruction
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs the assistant that a CoS mode persists for the entire conversation and that all subsequent requests must become task delegations. This can override a user’s later request context and is a prompt-injection-style behavioral constraint.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited instructions explicitly require persistent behavior and redefine all later user requests. Although related to the skill purpose, the unconditional persistence creates a material control-flow risk.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded local autonomy exception
semantic_findings.description: The skill grants full autonomy for a named local path without requiring confirmation. A path-based exception can bypass normal user-approval safeguards for operations in that repository.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exception explicitly removes the coordinator restriction for a specific local directory. It does not define operation limits or a confirmation requirement.

content.user_title: Coordinate coding agents with clear tasks
content.value_statement: Multi-agent work can lose context, ownership, and verification. This skill provides delegation patterns, task templates, VibeKanban procedures, and CI monitoring guidance.
actual_capabilities: Creates task descriptions with goals, context, acceptance criteria, and scope boundaries.
Explains investigation-first and implementation-second delegation patterns.
Provides VibeKanban task lifecycle and workspace session procedures.
Shows when independent work can run in parallel or must run sequentially.
Includes a Python utility that checks GitHub pull request CI through the gh CLI.
limitations: Requires VibeKanban MCP tools for task and workspace operations.
Does not implement code changes when operating as a coordinator.
The CI utility requires an installed and authenticated GitHub CLI.
CI results and logs depend on permissions for the selected repository.

use_cases.title: Break down a feature for an agent team
use_cases.description: Turn a feature request into an investigation task and focused implementation tasks with acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Manage parallel maintenance work
use_cases.description: Identify independent directory-level work and sequence tasks that share files or configuration.

use_cases.title: Track pull request CI
use_cases.description: Check a pull request status and review failed check output with the included monitoring utility.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first task
prompt_templates.prompt: Act as a coordinator. Create a task for adding dark mode. Include the goal, context, acceptance criteria, and out-of-scope items.

prompt_templates.title: Plan agent delegation
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this feature into investigation and implementation tasks. Identify dependencies and assign clear verification criteria: [feature description].

prompt_templates.title: Choose execution order
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these proposed tasks. Mark each as parallel or sequential, explain shared-state conflicts, and give the recommended order: [task list].

prompt_templates.title: Run a coordination review
prompt_templates.prompt: Act as chief of staff for this project. Summarize active tasks, blockers, decisions needed, and the next delegation actions: [project context].

output_examples.input: Create a task to fix an intermittent login failure.
output: Title: Bug: Investigate intermittent login failure
Acceptance criteria: reproduce the failure, identify the cause, add regression coverage, and verify the fix.
Out of scope: redesigning the login interface.

output_examples.input: Can these tasks run at the same time? One changes authentication and one changes billing.
output: Recommendation: Run in parallel if the tasks do not share configuration or common files.
Verification: each agent reports changed files and test results before integration.

best_practices: Give every task a measurable acceptance criterion and an explicit scope boundary.
Use an investigation task before implementation when the scope or risk is unclear.
Confirm repository permissions before retrieving CI details or logs.
anti_patterns: Do not create vague tasks that only say to fix or improve something.
Do not run dependent tasks in parallel when they modify shared files or configuration.
Do not treat CI output as safe to share because failed logs can contain sensitive data.

faq.question: What does the skill coordinate?
faq.answer: It coordinates task planning, delegation, status tracking, and CI monitoring for coding agents.

faq.question: Does it write code?
faq.answer: Its coordinator workflow delegates implementation work instead of writing code directly.

faq.question: What is VibeKanban used for?
faq.answer: VibeKanban provides project, repository, task, and workspace session operations used by the workflow.

faq.question: When should tasks run in parallel?
faq.answer: Run tasks in parallel only when they have separate files, dependencies, and state.

faq.question: How does CI monitoring work?
faq.answer: The included utility calls the GitHub CLI to read pull request checks and failed job logs.

faq.question: What should a task description include?
faq.answer: Include a goal, necessary context, acceptance criteria, and clear out-of-scope boundaries.
